_comment: THE benchmark matrix. Read by .github/workflows/bench.yml to plan its jobs and
by tests/e2e/233_bench_matrix.sh to check this file against the harness's own
vocabulary. bench/SPEC.md explains the axes; it deliberately does not repeat
the cell list, because a matrix written down twice is a matrix that disagrees
A cell is one CI job. Inside it the harness sweeps every engine x variant x
scenario, so those axes are per-cell lists rather than more jobs: they share a
checkout, a toolchain install and a fixture, and splitting them would multiply
runner minutes without adding a single measurement.
_baseline_note: Every ratio in every report is against cmake. See SPEC.md S2.

cells.note: bazel omitted: its module support requires a clang driver (see the bazel engine's unsupported_reason)
bazel omitted: same clang-driver requirement as the gcc cell
touch-leaf omitted: a real tree has no unit nobody imports that is also stable enough to name
mcpp-vs-mcpp is the point here (see projects/xlings/README.md); the cmake arm compiles all 110 units and is expected to stop at the link

excluded.reason: no gcc payload exists for macOS in mcpp's registry, and a Homebrew gcc would make the cell a comparison of distributions rather than of engines

mcpp supports x86_64-windows-gnu, but the other four engines would each have to be pointed at an msys2 gcc that mcpp does not use. KNOWN GAP, not a decision: the cell is meaningful and is simply not wired up yet
mcpp's own schedule policy reports msvc as unmeasured (src/build/schedule/policy.cppm), so the mcpp arm would be measuring a shape nobody has validated
same as the mcpp project on msvc
xlings has not been shown to build on Windows at all. KNOWN GAP: verify the plain build first, then add the cell — a bench cell that cannot build is not a measurement
